title: openai-compat: implement tool_choice semantics + schema mapping and tool message formatting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: make Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer fully interoperable with OpenAI-style function/tool calling semantics introduced as 'tool_choice' and standardized JSON-schema mapping for tool arguments. This PR implements: 1) tool_choice selection semantics (user-facing choice between multiple candidate tools returned by the model) with deterministic fallback rules and canonicalization for streaming responses; 2) schema mapping layer that converts OpenAI-style tool schemas to Redwood internal ToolDescriptor and back, including enum/oneOf handling and permissive parsing; 3) tool message formatting changes so that tool invocations in chat and streaming modes use the new messaging envelope (tool.name, tool.arguments as JSON string or structured JSON depending on client capability) and preserve assistant/tool attribution for observability; 4) compatibility shims for older clients (legacy_tool_field) to avoid breaking existing integrations. Includes comprehensive unit and integration tests, documentation updates, and changelog/release notes. Checklist: - [x] design doc (linked ENG-8421) - [x] proto/JSON schema compatibility tests - [x] end-to-end integration tests with openai-compat harness - [x] docs and examples updated - [x] added migration note for private deployments
commits: 3 commits: a1f4c2d - implement tool_choice selection and API plumbing; b7d9e11 - add schema mapping utilities + tests; d3b2f4a - update docs, examples, and compatibility shims
files_changed:
high-level file changes: 
- service/openai_compat/handler.py: add tool_choice parsing, selection heuristics, and streaming envelope handling (new functions: _handle_tool_choice, _stream_tool_invocation).
- service/openai_compat/schema_mapper.py: new module to map OpenAI tool schemas to internal tool descriptors, handle oneOf/anyOf/enums, and generate validation helpers.
- runtime/tool_invoker.py: adapt invoker to accept structured arguments or JSON-string payloads and emit standardized tool messages.
- runtime/tests/test_tool_choice.py: unit tests covering successful tool_choice selection, tie-breaking, and fallback to single-tool invocation.
- runtime/tests/test_schema_mapping.py: schema edge-case tests (oneOf, missing required fields, extra properties).
- docs/openai-compat.md: document tool_choice semantics, examples for streaming and non-streaming clients.
- examples/openai-compat/tool_choice_example.py: end-to-end example using SDK helper.
- infra/compat_shims.yaml: feature flag to gate strict schema enforcement for Private deployments.
- telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: add metrics for tool_choice_selected, tool_choice_fallback, tool_schema_validation_error.
discussion: Reviewer: Miguel Ortega: Can you clarify how tie-breaking works when the model returns multiple tool candidates with equal scores? Author: Tie-breaking uses deterministic ordering: explicit score > confidence meta > lexical name order; documented in openai-compat.md. Reviewer: Lina Chen: How do streaming clients receive partial tool arguments? Will partial JSON chunks cause validation errors? Author: Streaming uses an envelope that marks 'tool.arguments_partial': true for intermediate chunks; we buffer and only validate once 'complete' flag arrives. For clients that cannot buffer, we offer an option to receive tool.arguments as an escaped JSON string in a single final event. Reviewer: Arjun Rao: Any perf impact on hot path? Author: Minimal; schema mapping is memoized per tool signature and validated only on first encounter (cached), per-request overhead ~0.2ms median in our microbenchmarks. Miguel: please add an integration test that simulates an older client sending legacy_tool_field. Author: Added test and compatibility shim (infra flag).
